items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: I was studying with Joe Viola in Boston, a very fine saxophone teacher... I was a private student of Joe’s... He was the head of the woodwind department there and my goodness I studied with him for a long, long time. A long apprenticeship.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you about when two things happened for you. First of all, the soprano saxophone — when did that become your instrument of choice?

Well you know I think I was studying with Joe Viola in Boston, a very fine saxophone teacher. And soprano was a passion of his. So I can remember him pulling it out during lessons and stuff. I started with him when I was about 12 or 13, so I was exposed to it quite young. And when I heard him play it, I liked that. I want to play like that.
